description: 7.4 billion tokens per month. 34 free LLM providers. 635 free model endpoints. All behind one /v1 endpoint, plus any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Smart routing, automatic failover, encrypted keys. Personal experimentation only.

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted OpenAI-compatible router that pools free-tier LLM API keys from many providers behind a single /v1 endpoint, with routing, failover and encrypted key storage.
keywords: share one api key across apps
use free llm models in my coding agent
summary.what_it_does: The project exposes a single OpenAI-compatible /v1 API (chat completions, responses, completions, embeddings, images, video, speech, transcriptions, models) that forwards requests to whichever configured free-tier provider and model is currently best available. It also serves an Anthropic Messages surface, native Gemini and opt-in Ollama surfaces, and a "fusion" virtual model that synthesizes answers from several models. Provider keys are stored AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite, and clients only use one unified bearer token. A router tracks per-key RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD usage, retries the next model on 429 or 5xx with cooldowns, and offers several routing strategies plus named fallback-chain profiles. The README also describes a React dashboard for keys, chain ordering, playground and analytics, an MCP server, and an optional response cache and prompt compression. A paid "premium" tier provides a faster signed model-catalog feed; the README states the router itself stays MIT-licensed and free.
use_cases: Point an OpenAI SDK or coding agent at one local endpoint that spreads requests across free providers
Automatically fail over to another free model when one provider is rate-limited
Run Claude Code, Codex CLI or Gemini CLI against a pool of free models
Keep multiple free-tier provider API keys in one encrypted local store
Prototype or learn against free LLM tiers without paying per token
Connect a local model server such as LM Studio, vLLM or Ollama alongside cloud free tiers
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <install script URL from README> | bash   (Docker required; sets up ~/freellmapi and starts the container)
Open the Keys page in the dashboard, add provider keys, reorder the Fallback Chain
Copy the unified freellmapi-... key from the Keys page and set it as api_key with base_url pointing at your /v1 server
Dev setup: npm install && npm run dev (server on :3001, dashboard on :5173)
Optional: npx freellmapi setup-claude --url --api-key (configures Claude Code; see README for other agents)
notable: One OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint over many free providers, with an X-Routed-Via header showing which provider served each response
Per-key rate tracking that learns provider ceilings so routing stays under free-tier caps
Also speaks Anthropic Messages, native Gemini and opt-in Ollama wire formats
Virtual 'fusion' model fans a prompt out to several free models and a judge model synthesizes the answer
Desktop tray app for macOS and Windows, plus a dashboard translated into 60 languages
caveats: The README says it is for personal experimentation and learning, not production; free tiers have no SLA and variable latency
Free installs receive the signed model catalog from a monthly snapshot (about 30 days behind the live feed); the live feed is part of a paid premium tier ($19/yr or $49 lifetime)
Quality dips late in the day as top free models hit daily caps; no frontier models per the README
